title: Alaska Fire History (BLM AFS)
summary: Statewide Alaska fire perimeter polygons and ignition points from the BLM Alaska Fire Service.
provider: BLM Alaska Fire Service and Alaska Interagency Coordination Center
caveat: The record does not include every fire, and polygons are less complete than points. Some older polygons were flagged for geospatial inaccuracies. Check the download page for current file formats.

title: CAL FIRE FRAP Historical Fire Perimeters
summary: California fire perimeters from 1878 to the latest fire season, from CAL FIRE's Fire and Resource Assessment Program.
caveat: Updated each spring with the prior fire season. CAL FIRE says the record is the most complete digital one for California but still incomplete, especially before 1950. Inclusion thresholds can differ from NIFC data.

title: Canadian National Fire Database (CNFDB)
summary: Fire perimeters and point locations reported by Canadian agencies.

title: ESA Fire_cci MODIS Burned Area (v5.1)
summary: Global burned area pixel product with date of burn and confidence, from MODIS.
caveat: Also available as an Earth Engine collection. For recent years use the Sentinel-3 SYN product (2019 to 2024, about 300 m).

title: ESA Fire_cci Sentinel-3 SYN Burned Area (v1.1)
summary: Global burned area pixel product at about 300 m from Sentinel-3 SYN, with date of burn and confidence.
period: 2019 to 2022 (CEDA pixel record); the ESA catalogue lists 2019 to 2024
caveat: FireCCIS311. The v1.1 user guide lists 2019 to 2022 while the ESA catalogue lists 2019 to 2024, so confirm the years you need. Version 1.0 is superseded. The pixel product is GeoTIFF in 6 continental tiles. The 0.25 degree monthly grid is a separate record.

title: GABAM Global Annual Burned Area Map
summary: 30 m annual burned area from Landsat for the globe, built in Google Earth Engine.
provider: Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences
caveat: Zenodo v3 (December 2025) covers 2014 to 2024. An earlier record covers 2014 to 2021, and the Earth Engine community catalog lists 1990 to 2021, so confirm years in the files you download.

title: MODIS MCD64A1 Burned Area
summary: Global monthly burned-area product with burn date, from MODIS surface reflectance.
caveat: NASA plans to stop Terra MODIS science data collection in February 2027 and Aqua in September 2027 (LAADS DAAC). Earthdata describes shutdown as beginning in late 2026 to early 2027, with both orbits drifting. VNP64A1 is the VIIRS continuity product, but see its caveat on S-NPP.

title: MTBS (Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity)
summary: Burn severity mosaics and perimeters for large US fires, mapped from Landsat.
provider: USGS EROS and USDA Forest Service
caveat: Covers fires of at least 1,000 acres in the West and 500 acres in the East. Includes prescribed fire perimeters. See Prescribed fire & fuel treatments for other prescribed burn sources.

title: NBAC (National Burned Area Composite)
summary: Annual Canadian burned area polygons compiled from provincial, territorial, Parks Canada and satellite sources.
provider: Canadian Forest Service (NRCan) with provincial, territorial and Parks Canada agencies
caveat: The Canadian Forest Service asks users to cite the NBAC paper. Confirm the licence on the Datamart metadata. Year coverage and file names change with each release.

title: Southeast FireMap Burned Area (SE FireMap)
summary: Annual Landsat burned area for the southeastern US, covering prescribed fire and wildfire, with burn date and burn probability.
provider: USGS and Tall Timbers Research Station
caveat: Covers prescribed fire and wildfire together. The 30 m resolution can miss small burns. Vector polygons are released separately.

title: USGS Landsat Burned Area (Collection 2 Level-3)
summary: Scene-level burn classification and burn probability rasters from Landsat 4 to 9.
caveat: Acquisition-based products: each scene gets a burn classification and probability, not a fire perimeter. Order through EarthExplorer. The April 2026 data release (v5.0) covers the conterminous US. Collection 2 ARD exists for Alaska, but I found no Alaska burned-area product.

title: VIIRS VNP64A1 Burned Area
summary: Global monthly 500 m burned area with burn date from Suomi NPP VIIRS, designed as the successor to MCD64A1.
caveat: Version 2 was released in October 2024 and Version 1 was decommissioned on July 31, 2025. Uses 750 m VIIRS imagery with 750 m active fire detections on a 500 m grid. An Earthdata catalog page says delivery of Suomi NPP VIIRS science products ended on November 2, 2026. Confirm VNP64A1 production status and whether a NOAA-20 burned-area product exists before relying on it for new years. Earth Engine and the DAAC list different end dates, so check current coverage.

title: WFIGS Interagency Fire Perimeters
summary: Current and historical wildland fire perimeters from US interagency sources.

title: GOES-R Fire/Hot Spot Characterization on AWS
summary: Geostationary fire detection with fire power and temperature, updated every 5 to 15 minutes.
caveat: GOES-19 operational data production began April 7, 2025, and earlier GOES-19 data are provisional. NOAA advises users with low false-alarm tolerance to use mask codes 10, 11, 30 and 31.

title: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
summary: Near-real-time active fire detections from MODIS and VIIRS, with map, download and API access.
caveat: MODIS detections depend on Terra and Aqua. NASA plans to stop Terra MODIS science data collection in February 2027 and Aqua in September 2027 (LAADS DAAC). VIIRS detections continue.

title: NOAA Hazard Mapping System (HMS) Fire and Smoke
summary: Analyst-reviewed fire detections and smoke plume polygons for North America.

title: EFFIS (European Forest Fire Information System)
summary: Burnt area, fire danger and statistics for Europe and surrounding regions.

title: FPA-FOD (Fire Program Analysis Fire-Occurrence Database)
summary: Point locations, discovery dates, causes and sizes of 2.66 million US wildfires from federal, state and local records.
provider: USDA Forest Service Research Data Archive
license: US Government data, free to use. See the archive Conditions of Use.
caveat: 7th edition (FPA_FOD_20260615), published 2026. It replaces the 6th edition (1992 to 2020), which the archive marks as out of date. The archive page states no license, only that the data can be used without permissions or fees.
citation: Short, K.C. 2026. Spatial wildfire occurrence data for the United States, 1992-2024 [FPA_FOD_20260615]. 7th Edition. Fort Collins, CO: Forest Service Research Data Archive.

title: NIFC Wildfire Statistics
summary: Annual US fire counts and acres burned by year, agency and state.

title: California Prescribed Fire Monitoring Program
summary: Plot-level forest structure, fuel load and recovery measurements before and after prescribed fire at 36 California sites.
caveat: Check the Dryad record for current license terms.

title: GlobalRx
summary: 204,517 georeferenced prescribed burn records from 16 countries, with weather and environmental context for each burn.
provider: Hsu et al. (University of East Anglia and collaborators)
caveat: Coverage is uneven across countries because each source database differs in reporting.

title: Prescribed Fire Permit Records for Georgia and Florida
summary: Permit records for prescribed burns in Georgia and Florida with weather conditions on permitted days.
caveat: Tall Timbers maintains a larger 12-state permit database (2010 to 2020) that is not publicly downloadable.

title: USFS Hazardous Fuel Treatment Reduction (FACTS)
summary: Polygon and line records of Forest Service hazardous fuel treatments, including prescribed burning, from the FACTS activity tracking system.
caveat: Records planned and accomplished treatments reported by the Forest Service. Other agencies are not included.

title: Fireline Engagement from the NIFC Feature Service
summary: Quality-checked fireline locations, verified perimeters and containment success or failure for large US fires.
provider: USDA Forest Service Rocky Mountain Research Station
caveat: Fires under 1,000 acres are excluded.

title: ICS-209-PLUS
summary: Cleaned incident status reports from the US National Incident Management System, with wildfire-only and all-hazards packages.
provider: Tall Timbers, USDA Forest Service and collaborators (figshare)
caveat: Reports are self-reported by incident teams, so costs and sizes carry reporting error.

title: FEDS (Fire Event Data Suite)
summary: Fire event perimeters, new fire pixels and active fire lines updated about every 12 hours from VIIRS 375 m detections.
coverage: CONUS and Canada (Alaska and Hawaii through FIRMS when released)
period: Near real time, with static outputs tied to publications
caveat: Satellite-derived perimeters are less accurate than operational ones. For US incidents the official incident data give a more precise perimeter. Vector output arrives about 4 hours after VIIRS data reach FIRMS.

title: FIRED (Fire Events Delineation)
summary: Fire event polygons with daily spread estimates built by grouping MODIS burned area pixels in space and time.
provider: Earth Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
coverage: CONUS and Alaska (V2), with regional releases elsewhere
period: Nov 2000 to Sep 2024 (CONUS and Alaska, V2); the original US release covered 2001 to 2019
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 per the preprint. Check each CU Scholar record.
caveat: Event parameters differ between regional releases. Check the record for the version and MODIS collection used.

title: Global Fire Atlas
summary: Individual fire size, duration, daily expansion, speed and direction derived from MODIS burned area.
caveat: Fires smaller than 21 ha are not included. Direction is only given for multiday fires. The ORNL release covers 2003 to 2016. A Zenodo update (v20250411) moves to MODIS Collection 6.1 and redefines fire seasons. Its year range was not confirmed here.

title: GlobFire
summary: Global fire event polygons with daily progression, built from MODIS MCD64A1 burned area.
caveat: Based on 500 m MODIS, so small fires are missed. Earth Engine v2 lists 2001 to 2021 and the PANGAEA record lists 2000 to 2021. Check GWIS for later releases.

title: FIA DataMart
summary: Forest Inventory and Analysis plot, tree, fuel and down woody material measurements for US forests.
license: Free to use, no fees (US Government data). Cite FIA.
caveat: Public plot coordinates are fuzzed and swapped for privacy. The R packages rFIA and FIESTA download from DataMart. No license is stated on DataMart itself. Some catalogs label it CC BY 4.0.

title: GEDI Spaceborne Lidar
summary: Lidar footprints with canopy height, cover, vertical structure and biomass from the International Space Station.
coverage: Global, between 51.6 degrees N and S
caveat: Footprints are sparse samples along orbit tracks, not wall-to-wall maps.

title: Globe-LFMC 2.0
summary: More than 280,000 field measurements of live fuel moisture content from sites worldwide.
caveat: Version 2.0 adds more than 120,000 entries and more than 800 sites over the first release. Use the 2.0 Figshare record, not the 2019 one. Sampling is uneven across regions.

title: Insect and Disease Detection Survey (IDS)
summary: Aerial survey polygons of tree damage from insects, disease and other agents.
provider: USDA Forest Service Forest Health Protection
caveat: Aerial sketch mapping is subjective and survey coverage varies by year and region.

title: LANDFIRE
summary: Nationally consistent fuel models, canopy attributes, vegetation and fire regime layers.
caveat: LF 2024 is complete (CONUS released September 2025; LF 2024 Update ver. 2.0, March 2026). LF 2025 products are rolling out by geographic area since January 2026.

title: LCMAP Land Cover and Change
summary: Annual land cover, land cover change and spectral change products from Landsat time series (Collection 1.3).
caveat: USGS advises against mixing Collection 1.x versions in one analysis. 2021 is provisional.

title: LCMS Landscape Change Monitoring System
summary: Annual landscape change, land cover and land use from Landsat and Sentinel-2 time series.
coverage: CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and US Virgin Islands
caveat: Also on Earth Engine and in the LCMS Data Explorer. Extent and years differ between versions.

title: NLCD (National Land Cover Database) and Tree Canopy Cover
summary: Annual land cover, impervious surface and tree canopy cover for the conterminous US.
period: 1985 to 2024 (land cover); tree canopy cover to 2023
caveat: Annual NLCD Collection 1.1 (June 2025) added 2024 to the six annual land cover products. Tree canopy cover runs to 2023. Do not mix Collection 1.0 and 1.1 in one time series.

title: Rangeland Analysis Platform
summary: 30 m annual cover and annual or 16-day biomass for herbaceous, shrub, tree and bare ground.
provider: University of Montana, USDA ARS and partners
license: Listings conflict: public domain (USDA) or CC BY-NC 4.0 (community catalog). Confirm at rangelands.app.
caveat: Also on Earth Engine and through the rapr R package. Check the site for known processing issues in recent years.

title: RCMAP Rangeland Condition Monitoring
summary: Yearly fractional cover of shrub, sagebrush, herbaceous, litter, bare ground and tree for western rangelands.
caveat: Newer releases replace older ones. Do not mix versions in one time series.

title: TreeMap
summary: Tree-level model of US forests, made by imputing FIA plot data onto a 30 m grid.
provider: USDA Forest Service Rocky Mountain Research Station
caveat: Each pixel holds an imputed plot ID. Test fit before using it for applications the publication does not list.

title: USGS 3DEP Elevation
summary: High-resolution elevation, from lidar-derived DEMs to 1/3 arc-second national coverage.

title: CEMS Fire Danger Indices (ERA5-based)
summary: Global daily fire danger indices, including the Canadian Fire Weather Index, from ERA5 reanalysis.

title: CWFIS (Canadian Wildland Fire Information System)
summary: Daily Fire Weather Index maps, hotspots, and downloadable fire weather and danger data for Canada.

title: Daymet
summary: Daily 1 km gridded surface weather (temperature, precipitation, radiation, humidity, snow water equivalent) for North America.
caveat: Covers weather variables only. Fire danger indices must be derived.

title: ERA5-Land
summary: Hourly global land surface reanalysis of temperature, soil moisture, wind, radiation and precipitation.
caveat: Needs a free Copernicus account and API key.

title: gridMET
summary: Daily gridded surface meteorology, fuel moisture and fire danger indices for the contiguous US.

title: HRRR (High-Resolution Rapid Refresh)
summary: Hourly 3 km convection-allowing weather analyses and forecasts, including wind, humidity and temperature.
caveat: The Herbie Python package simplifies retrieval of individual fields. NOAA says HRRR is not retired with the RRFS v1 implementation. A retirement date has not been announced.

snippets.label: Python
snippets.code:
from herbie import Herbie
H = Herbie("2024-07-01 12:00", model="hrrr", product="sfc", fxx=0)
ds = H.xarray("TMP:2 m")

title: PRISM Climate Data
summary: Daily and monthly gridded temperature, precipitation and dew point for the conterminous US.
provider: PRISM Climate Group, Oregon State University

title: RAWS (Remote Automatic Weather Stations)
summary: Hourly fire weather observations from interagency stations, archived by the Western Regional Climate Center.
provider: Western Regional Climate Center (Desert Research Institute) for NWCG agencies
caveat: Public data are not quality controlled. A 2025 mailing-list post quoting WRCC says raw public access is limited to the prior 30 days, with older data on request and possibly for a fee. I could not confirm that on an official page. The R package RAWSmet downloads and parses WRCC data.

title: US Drought Monitor
summary: Weekly drought category maps for the US, with polygon, grid and statistics downloads.
provider: National Drought Mitigation Center (University of Nebraska-Lincoln), USDA and NOAA
caveat: NDMC says its shapefiles were modified from the originals. Use a vector dataset to match official statistics. Community GeoParquet mirrors exist.

title: WFAS (Wildland Fire Assessment System)
summary: National fire danger, fuel moisture and weather maps and forecasts from the USDA Forest Service.

title: GOES Geostationary Lightning Mapper (GLM) on AWS
summary: Lightning flash, group and event detections over the Americas from GOES-R satellites.
caveat: Detection efficiency varies with flash energy and viewing angle.

title: LIS/OTD Gridded Lightning Climatology
summary: Space-based lightning climatologies from the TRMM Lightning Imaging Sensor and the Optical Transient Detector.
coverage: Global (about 38 degrees N to S for LIS)
caveat: A climatology, not event-level data. Use GLM for recent individual strikes.

title: CAMS GFAS (Global Fire Assimilation System)
summary: Daily global fire radiative power and emissions of trace gases and aerosols.

title: EPA AirNow API
summary: Real-time and historical air quality observations and forecasts, including PM2.5 during smoke events.

title: FINN (Fire INventory from NCAR)
summary: Daily, high-resolution fire emissions estimates for chemical transport models.
provider: NCAR Atmospheric Chemistry Observations and Modeling
caveat: The FINNv2.5 documentation I could check lists input fire data through 2020 (README, February 2022). Confirm the latest year on the NCAR ACOM or GDEX pages. ACOM files are gzip-compressed comma-delimited text, one file per year.

title: GFED (Global Fire Emissions Database)
summary: Burned area, fuel consumption and fire emissions of carbon and trace gases, globally.
provider: GFED team (Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and partners)
caveat: GFED5 burned area has discontinuities in 1998, 2001 and 2003 where new sensor data enter. Use caution for pre-MODIS trends. GFED5.1 adds emissions for 1997 to 2022. GFED4s runs through 2025 at 0.25 degrees, but the site recommends GFED5 where possible and notes that after 2016 GFED4s emissions no longer come from burned area. Emissions years differ by version.

title: HRRR-Smoke
summary: Hourly smoke forecasts from the HRRR model, run with satellite fire radiative power as the emissions source.
caveat: Smoke fields are variables inside the HRRR GRIB2 files. A forecast is not an observation.

title: PurpleAir
summary: Real-time PM2.5 readings from a crowd-sourced network of low-cost sensors.
caveat: Needs an API key. Raw PM2.5 reads high in smoke, so apply a correction such as the EPA US-wide one.

title: CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS)
summary: Structure-level damage assessments after California wildfires.

title: NASA Black Marble Nighttime Lights
summary: Daily, monthly and annual nighttime lights from VIIRS, used to track power loss and recovery after disasters.
caveat: Cloud cover and smoke can hide lights on a given night.

title: RAVG (Rapid Assessment of Vegetation Condition after Wildfire)
summary: Rapid post-fire canopy cover loss and basal area mortality maps for US Forest Service lands.
provider: USDA Forest Service Geospatial Technology and Applications Center

title: USGS Post-Fire Debris-Flow Hazard Assessments
summary: Likelihood and volume estimates of debris flows in burned basins, with a national assessment portal.

title: Building-based WUI maps (CONUS)
summary: Intermix and interface WUI maps for the conterminous US built from 125 million building point locations, at several neighborhood radii.
provider: USGS, with University of Wisconsin-Madison SILVIS Lab
period: Buildings from a 2018 release; vegetation from NLCD 2016
caveat: Single 16.9 GB zip. Building locations come from a Microsoft 2018 product, so newer construction is missing. Check the record for the file format.

title: FEMA National Risk Index
summary: Expected annual loss, social vulnerability and community resilience for 18 natural hazards, including wildfire.
caveat: The wildfire score comes from a modeled hazard layer. Check the technical documentation before comparing with local risk assessments. In December 2025 FEMA said NRI data moves into the Resilience Analysis and Planning Tool, so links on hazards.fema.gov may change. Confirm the current download location. GAO reports that DHS plans no further routine NRI updates after folding it into RAPT.

title: Global WUI map 2020
summary: Global map of intermix and interface WUI classes at 10 m, with tables of WUI area, population and wildfire area by country, region and biome.
caveat: Version 1.1 on Zenodo. Tiles are 100 km on the EQUI7 grid. Overall accuracy is 79.6 to 82.0 percent.

title: SILVIS Lab Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) Change
summary: Housing and WUI maps for the conterminous US by census block, from 1990 to 2020.
license: Free to use, no fees (US Government funded). See the archive record.

title: Wildfire Hazard Potential (WHP)
summary: Relative index of wildfire likelihood and intensity for prioritizing fuel treatments.
provider: USDA Forest Service Fire Modeling Institute
caveat: Edition numbering and archive IDs differ. RDS-2015-0047-4 is version 2023. Confirm the newest version on the FireLab project page.

title: Wildfire Risk to Communities
summary: Landscape-wide wildfire risk components, including burn probability and exposure, plus a community-level web tool.
provider: USDA Forest Service Research Data Archive
period: 2nd edition (published June 2024); next national update planned for early 2027

title: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index
summary: Census tract and county rankings of social vulnerability from US Census variables.
caveat: Rankings are relative within the US, not absolute measures. The 2022 edition uses ACS 2018 to 2022 data and adds ZIP Code Tabulation Areas.

title: GlobPOP
summary: Global gridded population counts and density at 30 arc-seconds, fused from five population datasets.
period: 1990 to 2022 (v2.0); the 1990 to 2020 release is v1.0
caveat: Built by fusing GHS-POP, GRUMP, GPWv4, LandScan and WorldPop. Count and density versions are separate files. Confirm the current version on Zenodo.
citation: Liu, L., Cao, X., Li, S. and Jie, N. 2024. A 31-year (1990-2020) global gridded population dataset generated by cluster analysis and statistical learning. Scientific Data.

title: Bailey's Ecoregions and Subregions
summary: Hierarchical ecoregion domains, divisions, provinces and sections for the US, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.
caveat: Intended for national and large regional display, around 1:7,500,000.

title: EPA Level III and IV Ecoregions
summary: Ecoregion boundaries at Level III and Level IV for the conterminous US, with regional and state extracts.
caveat: Download shapefiles rather than relying on the PDF maps, which can differ.

title: NIFC Geographic Area Coordination Center (GACC) Boundaries
summary: Polygons of the 10 US geographic areas used to coordinate wildland fire resources and report fire statistics.
provider: NIFC and National Wildfire Coordinating Group
license: See NIFC Open Data item page
caveat: The service returns at most 2,000 records per query. A border area between Utah and Colorado changed in September 2024. The list of coordination centers is in the National Interagency Mobilization Guide. A separate simplified copy exists for zooming only, not for mapping.

title: PAD-US Protected Areas Database
summary: Public land ownership, management, designation and protection status for US lands and waters.
caveat: Check the DOI page before citing a specific release number.

title: US Census TIGER/Line Shapefiles
summary: States, counties, tracts, block groups, places, roads and water boundaries for the US.
caveat: Boundaries change each year. Use the vintage that matches your attribute data.

title: USFS Administrative Forest Boundaries
summary: National Forest and Ranger District administrative boundaries.
caveat: Not a legal land description. Boundaries can differ from other layers because of update timing.

title: Next Day Wildfire Spread
summary: Earth Engine-derived dataset pairing fire masks with weather, vegetation and topography for next-day spread.

title: Sen2Fire
summary: Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-5P patches labelled for wildfire detection and segmentation.

title: WildfireSpreadTS
summary: Multi-modal daily time series of active fire, weather, fuels and terrain for next-day fire spread prediction.

title: Global Paleofire Database (Global Charcoal Database)
summary: Sedimentary charcoal records for reconstructing fire history over thousands of years.

title: NOAA Paleoclimatology Fire History
summary: Tree-ring fire scar and charcoal records archived by NOAA NCEI.
